newsitem.title: TURKEY: Two more Turkish MPs quit, Yilmaz near majority.
newsitem.headline: Two more Turkish MPs quit, Yilmaz near majority.

text.p: Two more Turkish MPs quit a pro-Islamist alliance on Friday, bringing secularist Mesut Yilmaz only two votes short of the majority he needs to win a confidence vote in his coalition government.
Conservative True Path Party deputies Ismail Kose and Kubilay Uygun told a news conference they had resigned and defected to a far-right grouping.
The resignations reduced a pro-Islamist alliance to 275 MPs on paper, compared with 272 likely to back Yilmaz at the vote, expected within two weeks.
Istanbul shares jumped nearly five percent by late morning on rising hopes that Yilmaz can form a coalition to prevent an Islamist return to power.
Secularist politicians were to begin drawing up the Yilmaz government programme and working out the distribution of ministries on Friday.
Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan resigned a week ago under pressure from the military but he plans to get back into office in a coalition led by conservative Tansu Ciller.
